\section[aumentar]{aumentar — to increase, to rise}

\label{lesson:ES-C608-aumentar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the resource, then the Spanish for the measure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: aumentar}
\textbf{aumentar} — \textquotedblleft{}to increase, to rise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los precios aumentan cada año.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Prices increase every year.}
\end{quote}

Used for numbers that grow; \emph{subir} is more everyday.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aumentar} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{augmentare}, built on \emph{augere} 'to increase' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aumentar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aumentar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{aumentar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the resource, then the Spanish for the measure, then say \emph{aumentar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does aumentar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To increase, to rise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[disminuir]{disminuir — to decrease, to go down}

\label{lesson:ES-C608-disminuir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the measure, then the Spanish for to increase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disminuir}
\textbf{disminuir} — \textquotedblleft{}to decrease, to go down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El paro disminuyó en verano.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Unemployment went down in summer.}
\end{quote}

Like \emph{construir}: \emph{disminuye, disminuyó}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{disminuir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{diminuere} 'to make smaller', built on \emph{minuere} 'to lessen' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disminuir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disminuir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{disminuir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the measure, then the Spanish for to increase, then say \emph{disminuir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does disminuir mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To decrease, to go down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el aumento]{el aumento — the increase, the rise}

\label{lesson:ES-C608-aumento}

\section[el crecimiento]{el crecimiento — the growth}

\label{lesson:ES-C608-crecimiento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to decrease, then the Spanish for the increase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el crecimiento}
\textbf{el crecimiento} — \textquotedblleft{}the growth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El crecimiento de la ciudad es rápido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The growth of the city is fast.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{crecer} — to grow.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{crecimiento} is built on \emph{crecer}, inherited from Latin \emph{crescere} 'to grow' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el crecimiento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el crecimiento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to decrease, then the Spanish for the increase, then say \emph{el crecimiento} again

\section[la tendencia]{la tendencia — the trend, the tendency}

\label{lesson:ES-C608-tendencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the increase, then the Spanish for the growth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la tendencia}
\textbf{la tendencia} — \textquotedblleft{}the trend, the tendency\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Es una tendencia nueva.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is a new trend.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tener tendencia a} — to tend to.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tendencia} is a learned borrowing from Medieval Latin \emph{tendentia}, built on \emph{tendere} 'to stretch, to aim at' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tendencia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tendencia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la tendencia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the increase, then the Spanish for the growth, then say \emph{la tendencia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la tendencia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The trend, the tendency\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
